name: trend-report
title: Trend across updates
description: Trend of a P6 schedule across its updates: per update the data date, finish and its variance against the first and the previous update, units % and baseline planned %, SPI, critical, near critical and negative float counts, DCMA grade, failed checks and BEI, milestone slips and what changed between updates (read only). Use when the user asks how a schedule evolved over its updates or for a trend report.

args.name: updates
args.description: Project IDs of the updates, separated by commas (empty: give eps)

args.name: eps
args.description: EPS ID holding the updates, used when updates is empty

args.name: near_days
args.description: Near critical: total float up to this many days

template:
Trend of a P6 schedule across its updates (Project IDs {updates}, or the projects of EPS {eps} when no update is given): one row per update ordered by data date, with finish, progress, float and DCMA figures, the milestones of the latest update shown and what changed between updates, then fixed follow-up actions. Nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. t = p6_trend(projects=["{updates}"], eps="{eps}", near_critical_days={near_days}, limit=20): one row per update: finish, progress, float, DCMA, milestones and changes since the previous update. In projects=[...], write one list item per value of the argument updates (values separated by commas: "A,B" gives "A", "B"); leave projects out when it is empty.
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (eps, updates).

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- Give the call the Project IDs of the updates when the user names them, else the EPS ID; never both.
- rows.-1 is the last row of t.rows: the latest update shown. The milestone dates table and the actions
  are about that update only.
- The actions are the fixed sentences of report.md only.

files.text:
# Schedule trend across {total} updates

Updates from data date {first_dd} to {last_dd}, ordered by data date. Values of the last F9 of each update; read only: nothing was written to the database.

## Finish by update

Finish variances are working days of each update's project calendar, positive = later: against the must finish date, the first update, the previous update and the update's own project baseline.

[table: updates]

## Progress and float by update

Units % = actual / at completion units (labor and nonlabor); BL planned % = baseline planned units at the data date; SPI = earned / baseline planned units (n/a without a project baseline). Near critical = open activities that are not critical with total float up to {near_d} days.

[table: progress]

## Schedule quality by update

DCMA weighted score (points out of 100) and grade, the checks that failed and BEI (n/a without a project baseline), as the health check computes them.

[table: quality]

## Changes since the previous update

[table: changes]

## Milestones

Milestones followed (present in every update):

[table: milestones]

Their dates in the latest update shown, {last_project}, in the same order:

[table: ms_latest]

## Notes

[table: notes]

## Actions

Only the actions that apply to the latest update shown, {last_project}:

[if: last_stale]
- {last_project} was changed after its last F9: reschedule it in P6 (F9) before using its figures.
[end if]
[if: last_vs_prev]
- The finish moved by {last_vs_prev} working days since the previous update (positive = later): ask for the reason and review the critical path.
[end if]
[if: last_neg]
- Open activities with negative float: {last_neg}. Recover them: the schedule misses the must finish date or a constraint.
[end if]
[if: last_failed]
- DCMA checks failed: {last_failed}. Run the schedule quality audit on {last_project}.
[end if]
[if: last_cuts]
- Durations cut since the previous update: {last_cuts}. Run the update integrity audit to see which and ask for the justification.
[end if]
[if: last_removed]
- Activities removed since the previous update: {last_removed}. Check that their scope was completed or transferred.
[end if]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- Neither updates nor eps was given, or the call asks for one of them: "Give the Project IDs of the updates, separated by commas, or the EPS ID that holds them."
- The call says a trend needs at least two updates, or that the EPS holds fewer than two projects: "A trend needs at least two updates of the same schedule: give two Project IDs or more."
- The call says a project is not found: "Project <the Project ID of the message> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- The call says an update has no data date: "<the Project ID of the message> has no data date: schedule it once in P6 (F9), then run this skill again."
- The call says a Project ID is an EPS node: repeat its message and stop.
- Any other error of the call: repeat its message and stop.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. t.total = t.series.updates (every update of the series counted once).

If it differs, the database changed during the call: run it again once. If it still differs, say so and do
not publish the tables.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The updates keep the order returned (by data date). When t.next_offset is not null, the four update tables
  end with "Showing the first <returned> of <total> updates." and the latest update shown is the last row
  of the page, not the latest of the series: say so once.
- The milestone dates are those of the latest update shown, in the order of the milestones table.
- Every milestone of the milestones table is written "Activity ID - name".
- Failed checks are written with the names the call returns, separated by commas; an empty list is "none".
- A value the call leaves null is n/a: the first update has no variance against the previous one and no
  changes, an update without a project baseline has no baseline variance, BL planned %, SPI or BEI.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Trend across updates

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. t = p6_trend(projects=["{updates}"], eps="{eps}", near_critical_days={near_days}, limit=20): one row per update: finish, progress, float, DCMA, milestones and changes since the previous update. In projects=[...], write one list item per value of the argument updates (values separated by commas: "A,B" gives "A", "B"); leave projects out when it is empty.
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (eps, updates).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {updates}: Project IDs of the updates, separated by commas (empty: give eps), as given
- {eps}: EPS ID holding the updates, used when updates is empty, as given
- {near_days}: Near critical: total float up to this many days, as given

## Units

- wd: working days of each activity's calendar
- wd proj: working days of the project calendar
- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- %: percent
- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| total | t.total | count | int | n/a | updates in the series |
| first_dd | t.series.first_data_date |  | date | n/a | data date of the first update |
| last_dd | t.series.last_data_date |  | date | n/a | data date of the latest update |
| near_d | t.near_critical_days | d | n1 | n/a | near critical limit in days of each activity's calendar |
| last_project | t.rows.-1.project |  | text | n/a | Project ID of the latest update shown |
| last_vs_prev | t.rows.-1.finish_variance_previous_wd | wd proj | n1 | n/a | finish of the latest update shown minus the previous update's (positive = later) |
| last_neg | t.rows.-1.negative_float | count | int | n/a | open activities with negative float in the latest update shown |
| last_failed | t.rows.-1.dcma.failed |  | list | none | DCMA checks failed in the latest update shown |
| last_cuts | t.rows.-1.changes.durations_cut | count | int | n/a | durations cut since the previous update (as p6_update_integrity) |
| last_removed | t.rows.-1.changes.activities_removed | count | int | n/a | activities removed since the previous update |
| last_stale | t.rows.-1.stale |  | flag | n/a | the latest update shown was changed by this server after its last F9 |

## Table updates

Dates of each update; finish variances in working days of the update's project calendar, positive = later.

Rows: t.rows, in the order returned, at most 20.
When t.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> updates. (returned and total of t).
No rows: write 'No update.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| # | update |  | int | n/a |  |
| Update | project |  | text | n/a |  |
| Data date | data_date |  | date | n/a |  |
| Finish | finish |  | date | n/a |  |
| Must finish | must_finish |  | date | n/a |  |
| vs must finish (wd proj) | finish_vs_must_finish_wd | wd proj | n1 | n/a |  |
| vs first (wd proj) | finish_variance_first_wd | wd proj | n1 | n/a |  |
| vs previous (wd proj) | finish_variance_previous_wd | wd proj | n1 | n/a |  |
| vs baseline (wd proj) | baseline_finish_variance_wd | wd proj | n1 | n/a |  |
| Changed after F9 | stale |  | flag | n/a |  |

## Table progress

Progress and float of each update; float of open activities (LOE and WBS summary left out).

Rows: t.rows, in the order returned, at most 20.
When t.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> updates. (returned and total of t).
No rows: write 'No update.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Update | project |  | text | n/a |  |
| Units % | units_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| BL planned % | planned_units_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| SPI (units) | spi_units |  | n2 | n/a |  |
| Critical | critical | count | int | n/a |  |
| Near critical | near_critical | count | int | n/a |  |
| Negative float | negative_float | count | int | n/a |  |
| Min float (d) | total_float.min_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Median float (d) | total_float.median_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |

## Table quality

DCMA weighted score, grade, failed checks and BEI of each update, as p6_health_check with its defaults.

Rows: t.rows, in the order returned, at most 20.
When t.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> updates. (returned and total of t).
No rows: write 'No update.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Update | project |  | text | n/a |  |
| DCMA points | dcma.points |  | n1 | n/a |  |
| Grade | dcma.grade |  | text | n/a |  |
| Failed checks | dcma.failed |  | list | none |  |
| BEI | dcma.bei |  | n2 | n/a |  |
| BEI passed | dcma.bei_pass |  | flag | n/a |  |

## Table changes

What changed since the previous update (n/a on the first): activities by Activity ID, links, durations cut.

Rows: t.rows, in the order returned, at most 20.
When t.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> updates. (returned and total of t).
No rows: write 'No update.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Update | project |  | text | n/a |  |
| Since | changes.since |  | text | n/a |  |
| Activities added | changes.activities_added | count | int | n/a |  |
| Activities removed | changes.activities_removed | count | int | n/a |  |
| Links added | changes.links_added | count | int | n/a |  |
| Links removed | changes.links_removed | count | int | n/a |  |
| Durations cut | changes.durations_cut | count | int | n/a |  |

## Table milestones

Milestones followed, by date in the latest update.

Rows: t.milestones, in the order returned, at most 20 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 20 items, add the line: Only the first 20 milestones are shown.
No rows: write 'No milestone is followed.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Milestone | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Type | task_type |  | text | n/a |  |
| Updates holding it | updates | count | int | n/a |  |

## Table ms_latest

The milestones followed in the latest update shown (same order as the milestones table): date (actual else forecast), slip since the previous update and variance since the first, in working days of the milestone's calendar.

Rows: t.rows.-1.milestones, in the order returned, at most 20 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 20 items, add the line: Only the first 20 milestones are shown.
No rows: write 'No milestone is followed.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Activity ID | task_code |  | text | n/a |  |
| Date | date |  | date | n/a |  |
| Date kind | date_kind |  | text | n/a |  |
| Status | status_code |  | text | n/a |  |
| Slip since previous (wd) | slip_wd | wd | n1 | n/a |  |
| Variance since first (wd) | variance_first_wd | wd | n1 | n/a |  |

## Table notes

Rows: t.notes, in the order returned, at most 10 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 10 items, add the line: Only the first 10 notes are shown.
No rows: write 'No note.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Note | (the row itself) |  | text | n/a |  |

## Cross-checks (equal values)

- every update of the series counted once: t.total = t.series.updates
